message.content: {"summary":"You have written a competent ethics report that identifies key stakeholders, including Rachel, her company, the contract client, the health department and end-users, and links the dilemma to engineering quality. Your NHS and Volkswagen case studies give useful grounding. The main priorities are resolving the contradiction between your conclusion and recommendations, correcting the Volkswagen account, and adding an abstract and visual elements to strengthen the report's overall impact.","next_steps":["Rewrite your recommendations so they follow from your conclusion that not shipping is most ethical, and set out a recommendation for each stakeholder, including the health department and end-users.","Correct the Volkswagen description so it refers to defeat devices manipulating emissions tests on diesel vehicles, and flag your 1% failure figure as a hypothetical assumption, ideally supported by a sourced failure rate.","Add an abstract of about 150 words and at least one visual, such as a decision table or stakeholder map, and check that every reference has complete authors and a working URL."],"criteria":{"C1":"You identify a clear set of stakeholders and link the dilemma to engineering quality and business pressure, which is a strong start. To reach Excellent, describe each ethical issue, such as end-user harm and professional responsibility, in more depth and explain why it matters in engineering design. Develop how organisational context, such as commercial pressure and quality governance, shapes each stakeholder's interests.","C2":"Your case against shipping is developed with reference to the EACE code and external cases, giving your discussion a solid base. The case for shipping is thin and relies mainly on the Apple example, and parts read as opinion. To reach Very good, give the arguments for and against equal depth and objective support, then draw conclusions on how each stakeholder, not just Rachel, should decide.","C3":"Your sections follow a logical order from introduction to discussion to conclusion. However, your recommendations to accept the contract and delay launches contradict your conclusion, which weakens the argument. To reach Very good, make every recommendation follow from your arguments so the conclusion is clearly supported and the case feels compelling to the reader.","C4":"You draw on four references, including relevant NHS and Volkswagen cases and the EACE code, which shows genuine research. To reach Very good, add quantitative and qualitative evidence, support the competitive-advantage claim with a source that directly addresses it, and state clearly that your failure rate is an assumption. Correct the Volkswagen facts and complete the incomplete references.","C5":"Your report is organised into recognisable sections, but language errors, a missing abstract and the absence of figures or tables limit its clarity. To reach Very good, proofread carefully for grammar, typos and word choice, add a concise abstract, and include visual elements such as a table comparing shipping options. Format all references consistently and ensure each one directly supports an argument."}}
